title: Time-Transformed Test (STADF/GSTADF)
text: radf() (classic PSY GSADF test) assumes innovation variance constant. Real financial series usually don’t constant volatility, Harvey, Leybourne, Sollis & Taylor (2016) show volatility time-varying, radf()’s standard critical values longer control size – radf_wb_cv() already addresses exuber via wild bootstrap. radf_tt() implements different, bootstrap-free fix Kurozumi, Skrobotov & Tsarev (2024, Journal Financial Econometrics): instead resampling, time-deforms series using nonparametric estimate variance profile, deformed series behaves like constant-volatility random walk null. resulting statistic’s null distribution (pivotal) distribution homoskedasticity, ordinary asymptotic critical values apply – bootstrap, per-dataset resimulation needed.

title: Time-Transformed Test (STADF/GSTADF)
text: radf_tt_cv() gives matching (pivotal) asymptotic critical values; null distribution doesn’t depend volatility path, one call large n approximates whole family, unlike radf_wb_cv()’s per-dataset bootstrap:
code: set.seed(1) y <- sim_psy1(100) res <- radf_tt(y) res #>  #> ── radf_tt (minw = 19, kernel = uniform) ─────────────────────────────────────── #>  #>    series      adf   sadf  gsadf #>   series1  -0.7186  2.662  3.083 cv <- radf_tt_cv(n = 300, minw = 30, nrep = 1000, seed = 1) cv$gsadf_cv #>      90%      95%      99%  #> 3.248911 3.584415 4.246916

title: Time-Transformed Test (STADF/GSTADF)
text: hood, radf_tt(): estimates time-varying AR(1) coefficient local kernel regression, (truncated) residuals builds monotone variance profile eta_hat(s), s [0, 1]; inverts uses inverse resample/time-deform series; runs (GLS-demeaned, -intercept) recursive sup-ADF statistic deformed series – statistic family radf(), built need fitted intercept, matching paper’s derivation. kernel ("uniform", paper’s choice, "gaussian") h (bandwidth; default fixed plug-, paper’s full cross-validation search – see package’s enhancement notes cost/benefit reasoning) can adjusted.

title: Time-Transformed Test (STADF/GSTADF)
text: Kurozumi, Skrobotov & Tsarev’s footnote 4 gives exact published asymptotic critical value triple minw/n = 0.1: (2.319, 2.626, 3.223) (10%, 5%, 1%) levels – STADF statistic (single-sup, r1 = 0 case). exuber’s test suite (tests/testthat/test-tt.R) reproduces via radf_tt_cv()’s Monte Carlo checks lands within Monte Carlo/finite-sample tolerance published numbers.
